settings.title: Settings
settings.pairing_title: Pairing a device (once, on your own computer with the iPhone on USB)
settings.pairing_step1: Connect the iPhone by USB, open iTunes or the Apple Devices app and confirm 'Trust this computer'. This stores a pairing record on your computer: C:\ProgramData\Apple\Lockdown\<UDID>.plist on Windows, /var/db/lockdown/<UDID>.plist on macOS. A <UDID>.mobiledevicepairing file made by jitterbugpair works as well.
settings.pairing_step2: Enable WiFi access once: in iTunes / Apple Devices tick 'Sync with this iPhone over Wi-Fi' and apply, or run 'pymobiledevice3 lockdown wifi-connections on'. The iPhone must have a passcode set. Without this step WiFi backup does not work.
settings.pairing_step3: Upload the pairing file below without renaming it (the file name is the device UDID) and enter the iPhone's WiFi IP address.
settings.wifi_warn: The jitterbugpair file alone only enables WiFi debugging, not WiFi backup. You must additionally run 'pymobiledevice3 lockdown wifi-connections on' over USB once, or backups over WiFi will fail to connect.
settings.retention_helper: After a successful backup, snapshots beyond this number are removed (oldest first).
settings.device_ip_helper: The iPhone's address on the WiFi. The server must be able to reach it on TCP 62078.
settings.enc_password_helper: If set, backup encryption is turned on for this device on the first backup. Keep this password safe — it is required to restore.
settings.pairing_file_helper: <UDID>.plist from the iTunes Lockdown folder, or a jitterbugpair <UDID>.mobiledevicepairing file. Keep the original file name.
settings.no_devices: No devices yet. Upload a pairing file above.
settings.include_backups: Include device backups in the NS8 backup
settings.include_backups_helper: Off by default. The device backups can be several GB each and would roughly double this module's NS8 backup size; with it off only the pairing records and the device list are carried, so protect the backups separately.
settings.restore_warn_title: This overwrites a device and reboots it
settings.restore_warn: Restoring erases the target device and writes the backup onto it. Turn Find My iPhone off on the device first, keep it unlocked, on power and on WiFi, and confirm the passcode prompt. An encrypted backup uses the stored password.
settings.restore_no_snapshots: No snapshots for this device yet.
settings.restore_confirm_hint: The restore starts as soon as you confirm. It cannot be undone.
settings.ss_help: Let your users manage the backups of their own devices in a browser. They sign in with their directory account. Leave the host name empty to keep the module admin-only.
settings.ss_host_helper: Full host name for the portal, e.g. backup.example.org. Published through Traefik. Empty = portal disabled.
settings.ss_path_helper: Serve the portal under a path on that host instead of at the root, e.g. /idevice makes it reachable at host/idevice. Empty = at the host root.
settings.ss_stopped: The portal is configured but not running yet.
settings.ss_restore: Let users restore their own devices
settings.ss_restore_helper: Restore overwrites a device and is irreversible. Off keeps restore admin-only; users can still back up.
settings.ldap_enabled_helper: Users sign in to the portal with their Active Directory / LDAP account. Required for the portal.
settings.autobackup_helper: Back up devices automatically. An hourly timer backs up each device whose last backup is older than the interval; devices that are asleep are retried on the next run.
settings.autobackup_interval_helper: Minimum hours between automatic backups of a device (e.g. 24 = daily).
settings.run_waiting: Connection lost, next attempt shortly ({n} of {m})

ldap_login.no_domains: This cluster has no user domain yet. Add one in Domains and users, or enter an LDAP server.
ldap_login.group_helper: Only members of this group may log in (nested groups count). Empty: every user of the domain.
ldap_login.group_custom_helper: Group name or DN; only its members may log in. Empty: every user found under the base DN.
ldap_login.custom_intro: Only needed for a directory that is not a user domain of this cluster. NS8 can also add an external AD/LDAP as a user domain (Domains and users): then it shows up above and no credentials are stored here.
ldap_login.tls_verify_off: The certificate is not checked: someone in the network path could read the passwords. Only for tests or a trusted network.
ldap_login.bind_password_helper: Password of the service account; stored outside the module environment.
ldap_login.secret_is_set: A password is stored — leave blank to keep it.
ldap_login.ldap_domain_unknown: This user domain does not exist in the cluster
ldap_login.start_tls_with_ldaps: StartTLS is only for ldap:// URLs
